idiom_name: Fluent one-Model-per-table classes with property wrappers (Core Data entity inheritance for STI)
implementation_notes: Fluent has no inheritance mapping: every persisted type is its own final class Model with a schema name, @ID/@Field/@Parent property wrappers and relations declared per model, so a hierarchy becomes one model per table plus a mapper function that switches on a discriminator or follows a parent relation for the base row. Core Data is the counter-example on Apple platforms - a child NSManagedObject entity inherits its parent entity's attributes, which is the classic single-table mapper, and the framework instantiates the declared subclass - but server-side Swift has no equivalent.
pitfalls: Fluent models must be final classes with an empty init() so the framework can materialise rows; structs or value semantics lose the identity the mapper relies on.
@Parent/@Children load separately and lazily, so mapping a hierarchy through relations invites N+1 queries unless .with(...) eager-loads them.
Core Data entity inheritance hides a single-table layout: NOT NULL cannot be enforced on subclass attributes, and the entity must exist in the model or the row fails to materialise.
